context: Sales call for a team scheduling tool. Prospect: Granite Logistics, contact Hugh Mills, depot manager. List price: $9 per user per month, minimum 20 users. Pilot of 30 days is free. Customer references are available on request.

lines.text: Hi Hugh, thanks for making time. Nina, good to see you too.

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: Hello. I will mostly listen today.
Fine. Hugh, describe your current shift planning.

lines.speaker: Hugh
lines.text: We use a shared spreadsheet and a group chat and it mostly works for us.
A spreadsheet can work well for small teams.

lines.speaker: Hugh
lines.text: Honestly, nine dollars a user is too expensive for a team our size.
I hear you on price, let me think about the work it replaces.

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: We tried a scheduling tool two years ago and nobody on the floor used it.
Adoption is the real risk, I agree.

lines.speaker: Hugh
lines.text: My boss will never sign off on anything before the end of the quarter.
A pilot does not need a signature, that may help.

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: Our depot has bad signal, so anything cloud based is a problem for us.
I will check offline behaviour before I answer that.

lines.speaker: Hugh
lines.text: The other vendor said they would match any price you give us.
Let us compare the contents of each offer.

lines.speaker: Hugh
lines.text: The depot dog had puppies last week, the whole floor is distracted.
That sounds like a good reason for a distracted floor.

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: I will send you the shift pattern for one depot afterwards.
